reason: The passage explicitly reinforces strict hierarchical authority at multiple levels: God commands Moses absolutely (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה), Moses directs the people with decisive authority ('אַל־ תִּירָאוּ' - 'do not fear'), and Pharaoh's authority structure (commanding his chariot and people) is embedded throughout the narrative. The account demonstrates that proper hierarchical alignment (God > Moses > Israel) leads to salvation, while resistance to divinely-ordained hierarchy (Pharaoh's defiance) results in destruction. The text does not depict hierarchy as unimportant or discouraged—rather, it presents obedience to established hierarchical authority as essential to divine protection and victory.
